newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two dead, three injured in Pemex gasoline plant.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, three injured in Pemex gasoline plant.

text.p: Two workers died and three others were wounded in an explosion at a gasoline storage plant in northern Mexico City on Thursday, state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said in a statement on Friday.
Thursday's blast was the second deadly explosion at a Pemex facility near the capital in the last six months.
Four were killed in a blaze on Nov. 11, 1996, that sparked debate over Pemex's maintenance and safety measures.
Thursday's explosion occurred at 7:10 p.m. (1:10 a.m. GMT Friday) during drainage maintenance, a Pemex spokeswoman who declined to be named told Reuters.
"The explosion occurred away from the (gasoline storage) tanks and was totally contained," she added, explaining that the blast took place in a drainage area.
Regional civil protection Carlos Saenz said on Televisa's 24 Horas program late on Thursday that the walls caved in around 15 contracted workers at Pemex's eastern Satelite gasoline storage plant.
"The medical services of Petroleos Mexicanos reported that the state of health of the ... workers is stable," the statement said.
Pemex added that the plant was not damaged and that its refining arm had advised local authorities and would begin an investigation.
The spokeswoman declined to say if Pemex chairman Adrian Lajous would return from travels in the United States this week.
